subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Pocket Parks: Tiny Green Spaces
description: A fast breakdown of Pocket Parks: Tiny Green Spaces for builders.

hook.text: Paley Park in Manhattan is just 42 feet wide. It's one of the most beloved public spaces in the world.

buildup.text: Pocket parks are tiny — a vacant lot, a demolished building's footprint — turned into usable green space.

discovery.text: Paley Park's waterfall masks street noise. Twelve honey locust trees create a canopy. It feels like an escape.

twist.text: Research shows small parks get more use per square foot than large ones. People visit what's nearby.

climax.text: Cities now fund pocket parks strategically, targeting neighborhoods more than a ten-minute walk from any park.

punchline.text: You don't need acres. A few trees and a bench can change a block.

quiz.question: Why are pocket parks effective in dense cities?
options: They require less maintenance than large parks
Small parks get more use per square foot because they're nearby
They generate more revenue from events and vendors
